novelty_flags.label: Related work; Open-ended Question 1
novelty_flags.one_line: SunadaIzumi2025v2 Proposition 3.2 selects the unique minimizer of its penalty H over posterior-optimal couplings, and Theorem 3.3 proves average optimality; calling H an entropy penalty is inaccurate.

novelty_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed strict tightening is posed only against SunadaIzumi2025; add a second named capacity/minimax comparator or state a generic-class frontier to clear the flagship floor.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2
soundness_flags.one_line: “The capacity reduction is binary” is undefined, and the universal high-temperature constant 1/8 is not tied to a stated normalization of p, q, b, and Q.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4
soundness_flags.one_line: The asserted class of “coordinatewise positive linear-logit scalings” is not defined; only its common-scaling subclass C_lin is formalized.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 2
soundness_flags.one_line: A polynomial-time algorithm cannot output an arbitrary Borel equivalence class in D; specify a finite representation and evaluation model for the returned map.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 3
soundness_flags.one_line: “Six oriented edge-extension residuals” has no definition, formula, or indexed object, so the requested interval certificate has no determined predicate.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 5
soundness_flags.one_line: The final uniform diameter claim applies O_P to a supremum across different laws without defining uniform stochastic order or its probability formulation.

soundness_flags.label: ass:fixed-dimension
soundness_flags.one_line: It repeats the fixed-in-n declarations already built into the definitions of m and K; retain one source of the fixed-dimension restriction.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 2
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Existence and essential uniqueness of the global minimax map are explicitly assumed only as an upstream prerequisite.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Certified value and map recovery conditional on an affirmative answer to Open-ended Question 1.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 4
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The Gaussian existence and certificate conclusions are explicitly assumed as upstream prerequisites.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Expanding-local causal attainment conditional on affirmative answers to Open-ended Questions 1 and 2.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 5
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The global map, its certificate, and causal attainment are explicitly assumed as upstream prerequisites.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Joint policy-welfare inference conditional on affirmative answers to Open-ended Questions 1, 2, and 4.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 11–12, Proposition 3.2 and Theorem 3.3; footnote 8 on p. 12
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Proposition 3.2 selects the unique H-minimizer over Mopt(z), while Theorem 3.3 states average optimality. The paper notes that KL is not the chosen H because it is not continuous and bounded.
The published article studies nonlinear regret and derives finite-sample Bayes and minimax fractions for mean-square regret, extending the analysis to limit experiments.
The article develops semiparametrically efficient observational policy learning with application-specific constraints.
The preprint develops a locally asymptotically minimax statistical treatment rule under partial identification of the ATE.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications 494(1), 2021, article 124432
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article treats continuous entropic optimal transport, duality, existence, and primal-dual optimality conditions.
The article studies empirical welfare maximization with uncertainty in estimated budget implementation costs.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct the Sunada–Izumi comparison to its H-minimizing posterior-optimal selection and average-optimality theorem, and identify H precisely rather than calling it entropy.
Give finite encodings for coordinatewise scalings, edge residuals, and certified maps; state a uniform-probability definition for the inference diameter.
Add a second named published comparator or a theorem over a generic class of capacity-coupled decision rules, with a strict frontier against both comparators.
Normalize the scalar subexperiment explicitly, or replace the universal temperature endpoint by its geometry-dependent expression and prove its reduction under the chosen normalization.

recommended_next_step: Revise the formal predicates and corrected Sunada–Izumi comparison, then strengthen the global-minimax kernel with a second comparator or generic-class frontier before Stage 0.
